Copy link

Yes. When you buy a Flex Challenge you can turn on the daily loss limit option at checkout. The account then has a daily loss limit, and you pay less for it.

Flex without the option is unchanged. It has no daily loss limit in either phase.

The limit and the priceCopy link

With the option:

50K	$1,000
100K	$1,500
150K	$2,500

The option lowers the price of the account and of a reset. Prices change with our promotions. For the current prices, see the pricing page or ask us in chat.

Hitting the limit closes the accountCopy link

On Flex the daily loss limit is a hard breach. If your losses for the trading day reach the limit, the account is closed. It applies in the evaluation and on the funded account.

This is not how the daily loss limit works on EOD funded accounts, where reaching it pauses the account until the next trading day. Daily Payouts, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Instant work like Flex: the limit is optional at checkout and closes the account when hit. On Flex there is no pause and no second chance.

You choose once, at checkoutCopy link

The option can't be added or removed after purchase. An account bought without it can't be switched to the cheaper version, and an account bought with it can't have the limit taken off.

Resets keep it. If you reset a Flex evaluation that has the daily loss limit, the reset account has the same limit, and the reset costs less than a Flex reset without the option.

The rest of the Flex rulesCopy link

Everything else is in Flex Challenge: specifications, rules and payouts.

Should I take it?Copy link

Take it if you already stop trading early on a losing day, and you want the lower price.

Leave it off if a bad session sometimes runs deep. Without the option, a bad day costs you drawdown. With it, the same day can end the account.

Reach the profit target of 5% ($2,500).
Stay above the 4% ($2,000) end of day trailing drawdown, and within the trading rules below.

Evaluation: none.
Funded: 35%. It is checked when you request a payout.

Eligibility: 5 profitable days of at least $150 (0.3%) each.
Buffer: your balance must clear the $2,100 (4.2%) buffer plus the $500 minimum payout.
Minimum request: $500.
Maximum request: $1,500 per payout, the same cap on every payout.
Payout cycle: weekly, once you meet the payout rules again for each request.

Example. You start at $50,000. Once your balance reaches $52,600 or more, with 5 days of $150+ profit, you can request your first payout.

Profit split

80% to you, 20% to GFF.

Holding time: the 1 minute rule

When you pass the evaluation and at each payout request, both of the following must be true:

at least 70% of your closed trades were held longer than 1 minute, and
at least 70% of your net profit came from trades held longer than 1 minute.

If either is not met, we deduct the profit from winning trades held under 1 minute in that cycle from your payout and pay the rest. If that profit is more than the amount you requested, we decline the payout and deduct the requested amount from the account instead. This is not an account breach, and your account stays open.

News trading

Trading high impact news is not allowed, in the evaluation or on the funded account.

Overnight and weekend holding

Not permitted. All positions must be closed before the market closes.

Platforms

GOAT Access is available on DxFeed platforms (Quantower, ATAS, DeepCharts) and TickBlaze. NinjaTrader, Tradovate and TradeSea are not available on GOAT Access.

What happens if I breach?

The evaluation ends. You can reset for $39 or buy a new evaluation.

What is a trailing drawdown?
Copy link

A trailing drawdown is a loss level that moves upward as your account reaches new highs, but never moves back down. Think of it as a rising floor beneath your account. It follows your profits up but stays put when you give back. If your account equity falls to or below this level, the account is breached.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. This applies to all account types, both challenges and funded accounts. On most plans the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts and Instant (Instant Lite included) it is your starting balance plus $100.

There are two types of trailing drawdown at GOAT Funded Futures.

Trailing EOD (end of day)Copy link

Used on EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant accounts (Instant Lite included), and on Daily Payouts during the evaluation. The drawdown floor only updates at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
You close the day at $51,500, so your floor moves up to $49,500.
During the next day your equity dips to $49,200 intraday but you close at $50,800. No breach, because the floor is based on your end of day balance, not intraday equity.
Over time, your closing balances push the floor up to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Trailing intradayCopy link

Used on Daily Payouts funded accounts, and on Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026. The drawdown floor updates in real time, tracking your highest equity point during the session, including unrealised profits on open positions.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
Your equity reaches $51,500 during a trade, so your floor moves up to $49,500 immediately.
If your equity drops to $49,500 at any point, even before closing the trade, the account is breached.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Daily Payouts uses bothCopy link

The evaluation runs end of day trailing and the funded account switches to intraday trailing. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accountsCopy link

Once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

Updated 19 November 2026

What is the difference between EOD trailing and intraday trailing drawdown?
Copy link

The key difference is when the drawdown floor updates.

EOD trailing drawdownCopy link

Used on EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant accounts (Instant Lite included), and on Daily Payouts during the evaluation.

The drawdown floor only updates at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance. Intraday equity swings do not affect your drawdown level.

For example, if your account peaks at $52,000 during the session but closes at $50,500, the drawdown floor adjusts based on $50,500 only.

Intraday trailing drawdownCopy link

Used on Daily Payouts funded accounts, and on Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026.

The drawdown floor updates in real time as your equity reaches new highs, including unrealised profits on open positions. If your equity hits $52,000 even momentarily, the drawdown floor adjusts immediately and never moves back down.

Daily Payouts uses bothCopy link

The evaluation runs end of day trailing, and the funded account switches to intraday trailing on your highest equity. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article for what changes when you get funded.

Updated 19 November 2026

How does intraday trailing drawdown work?
Copy link

The Maximum Trailing Intraday Drawdown sets the lowest equity level your account is allowed to reach at any point during a trading session, including on open positions. It trails your highest equity point in real time, meaning as your account reaches new equity highs, the drawdown floor automatically moves up by the same amount. It never moves back down.

Only Daily Payouts funded accounts use intraday trailing. EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and the Daily Payouts evaluation all use end of day trailing, where the floor is calculated from your closing balance and only updates after the trading day ends. Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026 also use intraday trailing, as in the example below.

This is important to understand: the drawdown floor tracks your highest equity, not your closing balance. Even if you give back profits before closing a trade, the floor will have already moved up.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. On Instant Classic the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts it is your starting balance plus $100.

Example (Instant Classic 50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

Your account starts at $50,000, so the max drawdown floor is set at $48,000.
Your equity rises to $51,000 during a trade, so the floor moves up to $49,000.
If your equity drops to $49,000 at any point, the account is breached, even if the trade has not been closed.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Even if your equity later reaches $55,000, the floor stays at $50,000.

On a funded Daily 50K the same mechanics apply, but the floor locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accounts: once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your Instant Classic 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

What does "drawdown lock" or "DD Lock" mean?
Copy link
Important for Funded AccountsCopy link

The drawdown continues to trail normally as your account reaches new equity highs until it reaches your account's initial starting balance. Once it reaches the starting balance, it locks permanently and will not trail any higher.

On Daily Payouts, Instant and Instant Lite the lock point is your starting balance plus $100, not your starting balance. On a Daily 50K the limit locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100.

Requesting or receiving a payout does not automatically move or lock your drawdown at the starting balance. Your drawdown remains wherever it was before the payout.

Example

On a $50,000 funded account:

Current account balance: $51,000
Current drawdown floor: $49,000

If you request a $1,000 payout, your account balance becomes $50,000, but your drawdown floor remains at $49,000 because it had not yet reached the starting balance before the payout.

This means you now have $1,000 of remaining drawdown room.

Only after the drawdown naturally reaches your account's initial starting balance does it lock permanently.

Once the drawdown has locked, it will remain there even after future payouts. If your balance later falls below that level, the account will be breached.

Does requesting a payout lock my drawdown at the starting balance?Copy link

No. Requesting or receiving a payout does not change the position of your drawdown floor.

The drawdown continues to trail according to your account rules until it naturally reaches your lock point. Only then does it lock permanently.

If the drawdown has not yet reached the lock point before the payout, it will remain at its current level after the payout.

Updated 19 November 2026

Why does my funded Daily Payouts account use intraday trailing drawdown?
Copy link

Daily Payouts uses a different drawdown method in each phase.

Evaluation: end of day trailing. Your limit moves up with your profits once, at the end of each trading day.
Funded: intraday trailing. Your limit moves up in real time, tracking your highest equity, including unrealised profit on open positions.
What changes when you get fundedCopy link

In the evaluation, an open position that runs to a large unrealised profit and then gives it back costs you nothing in drawdown terms. Only the end of day figure counts.

On the funded account, that same trade permanently raises your drawdown limit at the peak. If the position reverses, the limit stays where it moved to.

Example: Daily 50K fundedCopy link

Your drawdown is $2,000, so from a $50,000 start your limit is $48,000.

You open a position. Your equity peaks at $51,400 while the position is still open. Your limit moves immediately to $49,400 and stays there.

The trade reverses and you close it flat at $50,000. Your limit is still $49,400. You now have $600 of room, not the $2,000 you started with.

When does it stop moving?Copy link

The limit stops trailing permanently once it reaches your starting balance plus $100.

On a 50K that means once your equity touches $52,100, the limit locks at $50,100 for the life of the account. From then on it never moves again, up or down, and your account can only be closed by falling below $50,100.

EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant Classic all lock at the starting balance, with no $100 added. Instant and Instant Lite use the same plus $100 lock point as Daily.

Does taking a payout move my limit?Copy link

No. Requesting and receiving a payout does not move or lock the drawdown limit. Your balance goes down by the payout amount, and the limit stays exactly where it was.

This matters most on the 25K. After a maximum $650 payout from the $26,100 minimum balance, you are at $25,450 against a floor locked at $25,100, which is $350 of room. On the 50K you would have $1,000, on the 100K $1,500, on the 150K $2,000.

How to trade with itCopy link

Two habits help:

Watch your peak equity, not your balance. The number that matters is the highest your equity has been, not where it closed.
Treat unrealised profit as spent. If a position runs $1,000 in your favour, assume $1,000 of your drawdown room has gone, because it has.

Payout requirements: winning days, first payout and request windows
Copy link

The requirements before a payout request depend on your account type. Most GFF plans use winning days and monthly request windows. Daily Payouts uses neither, and instead lets you request every 24 hours.

Requirements by account typeCopy link

EOD Funded	7	0.2% of the starting balance	None
1-Day-Pass-Plan Funded	5	0.2% of the starting balance	None
Flex Funded	5	Depends on the account size	None
Instant Classic	7	0.2% of the starting balance	At least 10 calendar days after your first trade and 7% account growth

What counts as a winning day?Copy link

A winning day is a trading day where your net P&L, after commissions and fees, reaches the minimum required amount.

For EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Instant Classic accounts, the requirement is at least 0.2% of the account's starting balance.

For example, a winning day on a 50K account requires at least $100 in net profit.

For Flex accounts, the minimum depends on the account size:

Flex 50K: $250, which is 0.5%
Flex 100K: $400, which is 0.4%
Flex 150K: $450, which is 0.3%

Winning days do not need to be consecutive. They accumulate until you reach the required number for your payout cycle.

Daily Payouts does not use winning days. Payout eligibility on Daily is based on time since your last request, your profit buffer, and the daily progression rule.

When can I request my first payout?Copy link

For EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Flex funded accounts, you can request your first payout after completing the required winning days and meeting all other applicable payout rules.

For Daily Payouts accounts, you can request 24 hours after you place your first trade on the funded account, with no winning days required. See how the 24 hour payout cycle works.

For Instant accounts, your first reward opens at 6% profit: $1,500 on a 25K, $3,000 on a 50K, $6,000 on a 100K, $9,000 on a 150K. There is no minimum number of days. Later rewards open at 5% profit per cycle: $1,250, $2,500, $5,000 and $7,500. Each reward is capped by the consistency option you chose at checkout: with 15%, $600 / $1,200 / $1,800 / $2,400; with 20%, $1,000 / $2,000 / $3,000 / $4,000 (25K / 50K / 100K / 150K). Rewards are requested within the payout windows, the same as our other plans (Daily Payouts is the only exception).

For Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026, all of the following must be completed before your first payout:

At least 10 calendar days must have passed since your first trade.
You must complete 7 winning days.
Your account must reach the 7% first-payout profit target.
You must meet the 20% consistency rule.
You must complete KYC verification.
What happens after my first payout?Copy link

A new payout cycle begins after each approved payout.

For Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026, you must also surpass your previous equity high, meaning the account equity level reached before your last withdrawal, before requesting another payout.

Additional recurring-payout requirements may apply depending on when your account was created. Please review the recurring payouts article before submitting another request.

When can I submit a payout request?Copy link

EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and Instant Classic

Payout requests are submitted through your dashboard during either of the monthly payout windows:

5th to 8th of each month
20th to 23rd of each month

If you become eligible outside a payout window, wait until the next window opens.

Daily Payouts.

There are no payout windows. You can submit your first request 24 hours after you place your first trade on the funded account, and one request every 24 hours after that, on any day of the month.

Before submitting your requestCopy link

Make sure that:

You have completed the required winning days.
You meet any consistency rule that applies to your account.
You meet the minimum payout amount and applicable payout cap.
You satisfy any recurring-payout requirements.
Your KYC verification is complete when required.

On Daily Payouts, check instead that at least 24 hours have passed since your last request, that your balance is above the profit buffer for your size, that at least half of what you are requesting is profit made since your last payout, and that your KYC is complete.

What are the requirements for recurring payouts?
Copy link

After an approved payout, a new payout cycle begins on the same account. You must meet the applicable payout requirements again before submitting another request.

What resets after a payout?Copy link
Your winning-days counter resets to zero.
Your consistency calculation starts fresh for the new payout cycle.

For your first payout, consistency is calculated using the profit accumulated since the account was funded. For later payouts, it is calculated using the profit accumulated during the new cycle after your previous approved payout.

New-profit requirement from your second payoutCopy link

For accounts created after August 7, 2026, the following rule applies from the second payout onward:

At least 50% of the amount you request must come from new profit generated since your previous approved payout.

For example, a $2,000 payout request requires at least $1,000 in new profit during the current payout cycle.

Without this rule, a trader could build a buffer from one or two large days and then keep withdrawing the maximum cap without making anything new.

Eligible exampleCopy link

You trade a 50K account to $54,000 and receive a first payout of $2,000, leaving the account at $52,000.

You complete the requirements for the next payout cycle and grow the account to $54,000 again. You have generated $2,000 in new profit since the previous payout, so you satisfy the new-profit requirement for another $2,000 request.

Not-yet-eligible exampleCopy link

Using the same example, your account has reached only $52,800. That is $800 in new profit.

A $2,000 request requires at least $1,000 in new profit, so you are not yet eligible to submit that request. Continue trading until the requirement is met.

InstantCopy link

After your first reward, each new reward opens once you reach 5% profit in the new cycle, requested within the payout windows. There is no winning day requirement. Each reward is capped by the consistency option you chose at checkout, see Instant: specifications, rules and payouts.

Additional requirement for Instant Classic (bought before 18 November 2026)Copy link

After the first payout on an Instant Classic account, you must surpass your previous equity high, meaning the account equity level reached before your last withdrawal, before requesting another payout.

If your Instant Classic account was created after August 7, 2026, you must satisfy both the previous-equity-high requirement and the new-profit requirement.

Daily PayoutsCopy link

The new-profit requirement above applies to Daily Payouts, where it is called the daily progression rule: at least 50% of what you request must be profit made since your last approved payout.

The rest of this article does not apply to Daily Payouts. There is no winning day requirement and no consistency rule on the funded account, so nothing resets between payouts, and there are no payout windows. You can submit your next request 24 hours after the last one.

What happens if my recurring payout request is declined?Copy link

A declined request is not a breach and carries no account penalty. Continue trading and submit another request once all requirements are met, during an available payout window on the plans that use them.

Before requesting another payoutCopy link

Make sure that:

You have completed the required winning days.
You meet the consistency rule that applies to your account.
You meet the new-profit requirement if your account is subject to it.
You have surpassed the previous equity high if you trade an Instant Classic account.
Your request meets the minimum payout amount and applicable payout cap.
You submit the request during an available payout window, unless you are on Daily Payouts, which has none.

What changes when you move from evaluation to funded
Copy link

Less than you might expect. One rule genuinely changes:

The consistency rule starts applying. There is none during the evaluation. On a funded account, no single day may be more than 35% of your total profit for the payout period.

Everything else carries over unchanged: the end of day trailing drawdown and its lock, your maximum drawdown amount, the daily loss limit and its percentages, contract limits, news trading rules, overnight and weekend holding, and the 1 minute holding rule.

Payout rules apply from this point too, since there are no payouts during an evaluation: 80/20 by default, payouts every 5 winning days, and 50% of your available profit per request with the rest staying in the account.

If you bought the 90/10 Profit Share Add-On with your challenge, it carries over automatically. There is nothing to re-purchase. Since there are no payouts during an evaluation, the add-on only affects what you take home once you are funded.

Why does 1-Day-Pass-Plan cost more than EOD?
Copy link

A 1-Day-Pass-Plan costs more than an EOD account of the same size. What the extra buys:

No consistency rule during the evaluation. EOD applies a 50% rule throughout.
Faster payouts. 5 winning days instead of 7.
A more forgiving funded consistency rule. 35% on 1-Day-Pass-Plan against 30% on EOD, so a bigger single day is allowed.
A 25K entry size, which EOD does not offer.

Two tradeoffs worth knowing before you choose:

1-Day-Pass-Plan has an optional daily loss limit which, if chosen, also applies during the evaluation. EOD has none in the evaluation.
1-Day-Pass-Plan tops out at 100K. EOD goes to 150K.

Can I trade during news events?
Copy link

The rules differ depending on the plan and on whether you are in the evaluation or funded phase.

During the evaluation phaseCopy link

It depends on the plan.

EOD, Flex and 1-Day-Pass-Plan: no news trading restrictions. You can open and close positions freely around any news event.
Daily Payouts: the 2 minute buffer applies during the evaluation as well as on the funded account. Daily Payouts is our only evaluation with a news restriction.
During the funded phase, all account typesCopy link

A 2 minute buffer applies around high impact news events. Within 2 minutes before or after a scheduled high impact news release, you cannot:

Open new positions
Close existing positions
Trigger pending orders

If a position was opened before the 2 minute pre-news window began, you are permitted to hold it through the event. See the news holding rule for more details.

This applies to all funded account types: EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant, Instant Classic and Daily Payouts.

What happens if you trade inside the windowCopy link

If you execute an order within the restricted timeframe, any profits generated will be deducted upon payout request.

Gap trading around scheduled earnings releases or other significant company-specific announcements is also prohibited and is treated in the same manner as high impact news trading.

What is the Path to Live?
Eligibility: How do I qualify for a live account?
What is the Path to Live?
Copy link

The Path to Live is how GFF rewards its most consistent traders with the next step in their journey: a live brokerage account, trading real capital that we provide. Once you qualify, your simulated funded account becomes a live account, you trade with real GFF capital, and you keep 90% of every withdrawal — with the freedom to request payouts daily and no per-payout caps. It is the opportunity to turn proven sim performance into a long-term partnership trading live. Any sim profit you have not yet withdrawn moves into your Profit Vault and unlocks as you profit on live.

Who is the Path to Live for?Copy link

Every GFF trader. The opportunity is open across every product, EOD Challenge, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant, Flex Challenge and Daily Payouts, and every account size. There is nothing extra to buy and nothing to sign up for: your place is earned purely through your trading on the sim funded account you already hold.

Why does GFF offer this?Copy link

Because we want to grow alongside the traders who prove they have a genuine edge. The Path to Live is how GFF backs its best performers with real capital on a live brokerage account — the structure used by the most established firms in the industry — and builds a lasting partnership rather than a one-off relationship. For you, that means trading real GFF capital, daily uncapped payouts, and a clear runway to scale your results over time.

Is live trading open?Copy link

Yes. GFF live accounts are open and the first traders are already trading real GFF capital. There is no launch date to wait for. Transition is decided by the risk team's review of your trading, so the best thing you can do is keep building a consistent track record on your sim funded account.

What happens between approval and activation?Copy link

Once the risk team approves you, we email you directly with the size and structure of your live account, the Live Funded Trader Agreement, any remaining KYC, and the onboarding steps for the live platform.

While your live account is being set up, your eligible sim accounts are held and trading on them is paused. This keeps the transition clean: your sim track record is locked in and nothing changes on it while the live account opens.

As soon as your live account is active, you are trading real GFF capital with daily uncapped payouts and a 90% profit share.

The email asks you to choose between going live and the 50% cash-out. Reply to the email with your choice. Your eligible sim accounts stay paused until you choose.

How do I qualify for a live account?Copy link

There is no public payout count, dollar target, or numeric milestone that "unlocks" a live account. Our risk team reviews every funded trader based on the full picture, meaning your consistency, how you manage drawdowns, your trading conduct, and your overall risk profile, and identifies when you are ready to move to live capital.

The best path to live is to trade like you intend to keep trading: consistent, disciplined, and risk-aware. Strong trading patterns are noticed regardless of payout count.

Why no public threshold?Copy link

We want traders focused on developing genuine consistency, not chasing a specific number. A public threshold encourages optimising for the threshold rather than for trading quality, which is the actual signal we look for. Removing it keeps the program aligned around the right thing: building the kind of track record we can trust on live capital.

What does the risk team look at?Copy link

The full picture of your trading with us, including but not limited to:

Consistency of your trading and your results over time
How you manage drawdowns and risk
Trading conduct, for example how you handle news, position sizing, and behaviour around the daily reset
Your overall risk profile and account history

There is no single metric that triggers transition. It is a holistic call by the risk team.

Can I ask the risk team to move me to live?Copy link

You do not need to. The team has full visibility into every funded account and reaches out directly when a trader is approved for transition. Asking for review does not move you up the queue, sustained consistency does.

Does my product type affect when I move to live?Copy link

The transition criterion is the same on every product (EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant, Flex and Daily Payouts): risk team review of your trading history. What can differ in practice is how quickly different products build a track record, since 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Daily Payouts accounts move faster per cycle while EOD needs more winning days per payout, but the decision itself is product-agnostic.

Do account sizes have different criteria?Copy link

No, the criterion is the same across 25K, 50K, 100K, and 150K accounts. The size of your eventual live account scales with your sim portfolio (see What happens when I transition from sim to live?), but the path itself is consistent.

Will my existing payouts count?Copy link

Yes, your entire trading history with us is what the risk team reviews. Every approved payout, your consistency, how you have handled drawdowns, your overall risk profile. If you have already built a strong track record, the risk team has visibility into that and factors it into their review.

How will I know I'm being moved to live?Copy link

We will reach out to you directly by email the moment your account is approved. Your transition notice walks you through the size and structure of your live account, the Live Funded Trader Agreement, any remaining KYC, and step-by-step onboarding for the live platform. Any payout you have already requested is paid as normal first. The email sets out both of your options, your live account or the 50% cash-out, and you choose by replying to it.

Affiliate Program
Copy link

You earn commission on every sale made through your affiliate link. You also earn 5% of the sales made by affiliates you invite, called sub-affiliates.

How to joinCopy link

Apply on our Affiliate Program page. Our team reviews every application. Once you're approved, you'll get your affiliate link and your invite link.

Your commissionCopy link
12% on your sales until you have referred 100 different customers.
15% on every sale from your 100th customer onward.

The 100 counts different customers, not purchases. If one customer buys three accounts within 30 days of clicking your link, each purchase earns commission, but that customer counts once toward the 100. Customers you referred before the new rates also count.

Challenge purchases and add-ons earn commission. Resets don't.

Commission is calculated on the price the customer paid, after any discount. Your own purchases don't earn commission.

There is no separate rate for your first sale.

Sub-affiliate commissionCopy link

Invite other creators, influencers or traders to apply to the affiliate program with your invite link. Everyone who is approved after applying through it becomes your sub-affiliate, and you earn 5% of the full amount of every sale they make.

Your sub-affiliates still earn their own full 12% or 15% on those sales. Your 5% doesn't come out of their commission.

You earn the 5% for as long as your sub-affiliate's account stays active. If their affiliate account is disabled for any reason, including fraud, the 5% stops.

Someone only becomes your sub-affiliate by applying through your invite link. An affiliate who already joined without it can't be linked to you unless they apply again through your link.

There is no limit on how many sub-affiliates you can invite. The 5% covers one level only, so you don't earn on affiliates that your sub-affiliates invite.

Your invite link is in your affiliate dashboard.

ExampleCopy link

Say you invite 10 creators and each of them makes $2,000 in sales this month. That's $20,000 in total, and 5% of it is $1,000 for you, without selling anything extra yourself.

SUB-AFFILIATES	SALES EACH PER MONTH	TOTAL SALES	YOUR 5%
5	$2,000	$10,000	$500
10	$2,000	$20,000	$1,000
10	$10,000	$100,000	$5,000
20	$10,000	$200,000	$10,000

If your sub-affiliates grow and sell more, your 5% grows with them.

When you can request your commissionCopy link

You can request a commission 30 days after it's credited to your account. Each commission has its own 30 days. For example, commission credited on 13 November can be requested from 13 December.

The minimum payout request is $100. You need to complete identity verification (KYC) before your first payout. Payouts are sent by crypto or Skrill and usually take 2 days to process.

Cookie trackingCopy link

We use a 30-day cookie. If someone clicks your link and buys within 30 days, the sale counts toward your commission. Purchases after those 30 days don't count. For example, if someone clicks your link and buys on day 29 and again on day 31, only the first purchase earns commission.

Refunds and chargebacksCopy link

If a sale you referred is refunded or charged back, the commission on it is removed, even if its 30 days have already passed. If it was already paid out, it's deducted from your balance.

We may disable the affiliate account of affiliates with a high number of refunds or chargebacks.

Why does my funded Daily Payouts account use intraday trailing drawdown?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

Daily Payouts uses a different drawdown method in each phase.

Evaluation: end of day trailing. Your limit moves up with your profits once, at the end of each trading day.
Funded: intraday trailing. Your limit moves up in real time, tracking your highest equity, including unrealised profit on open positions.
What changes when you get funded
Copy link

In the evaluation, an open position that runs to a large unrealised profit and then gives it back costs you nothing in drawdown terms. Only the end of day figure counts.

On the funded account, that same trade permanently raises your drawdown limit at the peak. If the position reverses, the limit stays where it moved to.

Example: Daily 50K funded
Copy link

Your drawdown is $2,000, so from a $50,000 start your limit is $48,000.

You open a position. Your equity peaks at $51,400 while the position is still open. Your limit moves immediately to $49,400 and stays there.

The trade reverses and you close it flat at $50,000. Your limit is still $49,400. You now have $600 of room, not the $2,000 you started with.

When does it stop moving?
Copy link

The limit stops trailing permanently once it reaches your starting balance plus $100.

On a 50K that means once your equity touches $52,100, the limit locks at $50,100 for the life of the account. From then on it never moves again, up or down, and your account can only be closed by falling below $50,100.

EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant Classic all lock at the starting balance, with no $100 added. Instant and Instant Lite use the same plus $100 lock point as Daily.

Does taking a payout move my limit?
Copy link

No. Requesting and receiving a payout does not move or lock the drawdown limit. Your balance goes down by the payout amount, and the limit stays exactly where it was.

This matters most on the 25K. After a maximum $650 payout from the $26,100 minimum balance, you are at $25,450 against a floor locked at $25,100, which is $350 of room. On the 50K you would have $1,000, on the 100K $1,500, on the 150K $2,000.

How to trade with it
Copy link

Two habits help:

Watch your peak equity, not your balance. The number that matters is the highest your equity has been, not where it closed.
Treat unrealised profit as spent. If a position runs $1,000 in your favour, assume $1,000 of your drawdown room has gone, because it has.
Which plans use which method
Copy link
PLAN	EVALUATION	FUNDED
Daily Payouts	End of day trailing	Intraday trailing
EOD Challenge	End of day trailing	End of day trailing
1-Day-Pass-Plan	End of day trailing	End of day trailing
Flex Challenge	End of day trailing	End of day trailing
Instant	No evaluation	End of day trailing
Instant Classic	No evaluation	Intraday trailing
Instant Lite	No evaluation	End of day trailing

Help Center / Rewards and payouts / How the 24 hour payout cycle works on Daily Payouts
How the 24 hour payout cycle works on Daily Payouts

Updated 10 November 2026Copy link

Daily Payouts is the only GFF plan where payout requests are not tied to a monthly window or to a winning day count. Here is how the cycle actually works.

Your first request
Copy link

You can submit your first payout request 24 hours after you place your first trade on the funded account. The clock starts when that trade is placed, not when it closes.

There is no minimum number of trading days, no winning day requirement, and no waiting for a monthly window. What you do need is:

A balance at or above the profit buffer for your account size
A request of at least $500
Completed KYC verification
Every request after that
Copy link

One request every 24 hours. There is no cap on how many payouts you can take.

Buffer, minimum and maximum

ACCOUNT SIZE	PROFIT BUFFER	MINIMUM BALANCE TO REQUEST	MAXIMUM PER PAYOUT
25K	$1,100	$26,100	$650
50K	$2,100	$52,100	$1,000
100K	$3,100	$103,100	$1,500
150K	$4,600	$154,600	$2,500

The buffer stays in the account and is not withdrawable. Profit above the per-payout maximum stays in the account too, and supports your equity going into the next request.

The minimum request is $500 on every size.

Two checks run on every request
Copy link

Both are checked when you submit, and a request can fail either one:

The daily progression rule.
At least 50% of what you request must be profit made since your last approved payout.
The 1 minute holding rule.
At least 70% of your closed trades and at least 70% of your net profit since your last payout must come from trades held longer than 1 minute.
What "50% must be new profit" means in practice
Copy link

You can request up to twice the profit you have made since your last approved payout, within the minimum and maximum for your size.

Worked example on a funded Daily 50K: Your balance is $53,400, which is $1,300 above the $52,100 buffer. Your last payout was approved yesterday and you have made $700 since. Twice $700 is $1,400, but the 50K maximum is $1,000, so you request $1,000. At the 90/10 split you receive $900, less the 3% processing fee, so $873 arrives. Your balance becomes $52,400.

The practical effect is that one very good day followed by flat days will not let you keep withdrawing. Each request has to be at least half funded by profit made since the last one.

Why was my request declined?
Copy link

A declined request is not a breach. Your account stays open and you keep trading.

The usual reasons:

Less than half the requested amount is profit made since your last payout. Keep trading and request again once it is.
Less than 70% of your closed trades, or less than 70% of your net profit, since the last payout came from trades held longer than 1 minute. In this case the profit from trades held under 1 minute in that period is also deducted.
Your balance is below the profit buffer for your size.
You requested less than $500, or more than the maximum for your size.
KYC is not complete.
Processing time and fees
Copy link

Payouts are processed within 2 business days of the request. A 3% processing fee is deducted to cover payment and transaction costs, so the amount that reaches you is slightly below the figure on your payout certificate.

How this compares to our other plans

	DAILY PAYOUTS	FLEX	EOD
Request frequency	Every 24 hours	Two windows a month	Two windows a month
Winning days needed	None	5	7
Profit split	90/10 from the first payout	80/20, 90/10 as a paid add-on	80/20, 90/10 as a paid add-on
Maximum per request (50K)	$1,000	50% of profit, up to $2,000	50% of profit, up to $1,500 first payout

Flex pays more per request. Daily pays more often, and at a better split without an add-on.

What is the daily progression rule on Daily Payouts?

Updated 9 November 2026Copy link

On Daily Payouts, at least 50% of every payout request must be profit generated since your last approved payout.

Turn that around and it is easier to use: you can request up to twice the profit you have made since your last payout. The minimum of $500 and the maximum for your account size still apply on top.

For your first payout there is nothing to compare against, so all profit above the buffer counts as new profit.

You may have met this rule before
Copy link

If you hold an EOD, Flex or Instant Classic account created after 7 August 2026, this is the same new-profit requirement described in our recurring payouts article. The rule is identical. The only difference on Daily is the cadence: instead of applying between monthly payout windows, it applies between requests that can be 24 hours apart.

Why it exists
Copy link

Without it, a trader could build a buffer from one or two large days and then keep withdrawing the maximum every 24 hours while making nothing new. The rule ties the pace of your payouts to the pace of your trading, which is the point of a daily payout product.

Worked examples on the Daily 50K Plan

Buffer $2,100, minimum balance to request $52,100, maximum per payout $1,000.

You made $700 since your last payout.

Twice $700 is $1,400. The 50K cap is $1,000. You can request up to $1,000.

You made $300 since your last payout.

Twice $300 is $600. That is above the $500 minimum, so you can request between $500 and $600.

You made $200 since your last payout.

Twice $200 is $400, which is below the $500 minimum. You cannot request yet. Keep trading until you have made at least $250 since your last payout.

You made nothing since your last payout, but your balance is $54,000.

There is no new profit, so nothing can be requested, however far above the buffer your balance sits. The extra profit stays in the account and supports your equity.

What happens if I do not meet it
Copy link

The request is declined. This is not a breach, no profit is deducted under this rule, and your account stays open. Keep trading and submit a new request once at least half of the amount you want is profit made since your last payout.

This is not the same as the 1 minute rule
Copy link

Both are checked at payout request and both look at your profit since your last payout, so they are easy to confuse.

The progression rule is about when the profit was made. At least half of your request has to come from profit made since the last payout.
The 1 minute rule is about how the profit was made. At least 70% of your closed trades and at least 70% of your net profit since the last payout have to come from trades held longer than 1 minute. Failing this one also deducts the profit from trades held under 1 minute.

A request has to satisfy both.

Copying your own trades is allowedCopy link

You may copy your own trades across your own GFF accounts, and across accounts you hold elsewhere. If you buy a multi account bundle, copying your own trades into each of them is the intended use.

Holding time rules on each plan

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

Since Monday 9 November 2026, every GFF plan uses one holding time rule: the 1 minute rule. The 2 minute microscalping rule no longer applies on any plan.

The 1 minute rule
Copy link

At each payout request, both of the following must be true for that payout cycle:

at least 70% of your closed trades were held longer than 1 minute, and
at least 70% of your net profit came from trades held longer than 1 minute.

If either is not met, we deduct the profit from winning trades held under 1 minute in that cycle from your payout and pay the rest. If that profit is more than the amount you requested, we decline the payout and deduct the requested amount from the account instead. This is not an account breach, and your account stays open.

The same check applies when you pass an evaluation. A partial close counts as its own closed trade, even if the rest of the position is still running.

Which plans it applies to
Copy link

All of them: EOD Challenge, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex Challenge, Daily Payouts, Instant, Instant Classic, Instant Lite and GOAT Access. It applies to new and existing accounts.

It does not apply on live accounts after the transition. There, we ask you to trade with the care of managing actual live capital.

What changed on 9 November
Copy link
EOD Challenge, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant Classic and Instant Lite: profit from trades closed within 2 minutes is no longer deducted trade by trade. The 1 minute rule is checked at payout instead.
Flex Challenge: the threshold rises from 50% to 70%.
Daily Payouts: the 60 second rule becomes the 1 minute rule. It now checks both your closed trades and your net profit, at 70%.
GOAT Access: uses the same 1 minute rule as every plan.

Trading and payout cycles up to Sunday 8 November follow the previous rules, including the 2 minute microscalping deduction.

Tick scalping
Copy link

Opening and closing positions within seconds to capture small tick profits, typically $10 to $50 a time, is not permitted on any account. Profit generated this way may be reviewed and deducted.

Why this rule exists
Copy link

So that results reflect what would realistically be executable on a live exchange, where slippage, partial fills and liquidity limits apply.

It should not be confused with the 2 minute news buffer, which is a separate restriction around high impact news events and has not changed.

Can I trade on TradeSea?

Updated 21 October 2026Copy link

Yes. TradeSea is available on every plan. It is a futures trading platform that runs in your browser, with TradingView charts, a DOM, bracket orders and built-in risk settings. It also has apps on the Apple App Store and Google Play.

Choosing TradeSea at checkout
Copy link

At checkout, under Select provider, choose Tradesea. TradeSea is its own provider, separate from CQG, DxFeed and TickBlaze Market Data.

As with every provider, you cannot move an account to or from TradeSea after purchase. Make sure it is the platform you want before you pay.

Your login details
Copy link

After payment you receive an email with your username, password and server, and a link to log in to TradeSea. Keep this email. You need it to connect.

Connecting your account
Copy link
Open the TradeSea link in your email. Sign in with Google, or with your email address. If you use email, TradeSea sends you a one-time code.
Open the Account Centre and click Connect New.
Find Goat Funded Futures in the list and click Connect.
Enter the username and password from your email exactly as given. If TradeSea asks for a server or environment, choose the one named in your email.
Click Connect. Your account now shows as Connected in the Account Centre.
If the connection fails
Copy link
Your credentials are rejected. Usernames and passwords are case-sensitive, so copy and paste them from the email. Use the login from the credentials email, not your GFF dashboard login.
Goat Funded Futures is not in the list. Contact our support team with your account ID.
The account says Connected but does not appear. Refresh the page, reopen Station, and pick the account from the selector in the top-left corner.

If none of these fixes it, contact our support team with your account ID and a screenshot of the error.

Market data
Copy link

TradeSea comes with free top of the book (L1) market data for the full CME bundle, the same as CQG. That covers CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX, so metals and energy are included without asking us to add them.

Other Rithmic platforms
Copy link

Your TradeSea login is a Rithmic login. It also works on other Rithmic platforms, such as Sierra Chart and R|Trader Pro, as long as the platform lists our server, GOAT FundedFutures. If a platform does not list it, that platform cannot connect to your account.

Copy trading with SecureCopy
Copy link

TradeSea has its own copier, SecureCopy. You can use it to copy trades between your own accounts. Copying another trader is not allowed, on TradeSea or anywhere else.

SecureCopy copies one leader account to up to 10 follower accounts per group, with up to 3 groups. Your plan's copy limits still apply. Daily Payouts accounts can only copy to and from other Daily Payouts accounts. Instant Lite allows copying across up to 3 accounts of the same program and size.

Two SecureCopy settings need care:

Multipliers. Each follower can copy at 1x, 2x or 3x the leader's size. A follower at 2x places twice as many contracts as the leader, so check that every follower stays inside the contract limit for its plan and size.
Risk settings on followers. Saving a copy group clears the daily loss, daily profit and position bracket settings on the follower accounts in TradeSea. Your GFF rules do not change. We still enforce your daily loss limit and drawdown on every account.

SecureCopy runs on TradeSea's servers, so it keeps copying after you close the browser tab. That is allowed and does not count as a VPS.

See Signals, copy trading and automated strategies for the full rules.

Mobile
Copy link

Connect your account on the web first. Then sign in to the TradeSea app with the same TradeSea login.

Transition: What happens when I transition from sim to live?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

What happens to my sim account when I transition?
Copy link

Your sim account closes and a fresh live account opens. Any profit you have not yet withdrawn from sim moves into your Profit Vault. For every $10,000 of profit you make on live, $1,000 is unlocked from the vault and paid to you, until the vault is empty.

What if I have multiple sim accounts?
Copy link

Great news if you trade more than one account: when the risk team approves you for transition, every sim account that has taken at least one approved payout is combined into a single live account with you. Your live account size is determined by summing your eligible sim account sizes, capped at 150K — GFF's largest live tier.

A few examples:

1× 50K → 50K Live ($2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown)
2× 25K 1-Day-Pass-Plan → 50K Live ($2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown)
3× 50K → 150K Live ($4,500 end-of-day trailing drawdown)
1× 100K + 1× 150K → 150K Live ($4,500 end-of-day trailing drawdown)

Any sim account that has not taken a payout yet is simply closed and its account fee refunded to you.

Unwithdrawn profit from every account that is combined into your live account goes into one Profit Vault.

If you choose the 50% cash-out instead of going live, it is based on your combined live size. Example: three 50K accounts make a 150K Live, so the cash-out is $2,250.

Why do all my eligible accounts move to live together?
Copy link

Because once you have proven yourself, we want your whole book on live — not just one account. Combining every eligible account into your live account means your full track record is rewarded at once, with your sim sizes adding together (up to the 150K cap) to give you the biggest possible live account to trade.

Do I have to trade live once I'm approved?
Copy link

No. Once you are approved, you choose one of two options:

Go live: trade a live account with real GFF capital, daily uncapped payouts and a 90% profit share.
Cash out: take 50% of your live drawdown as an instant payout instead of trading live. A 21-day cooldown starts straight away.

Cash-out amounts: 50K Live $1,000 · 100K Live $1,500 · 150K Live $2,250.

The cash-out is optional. Staying on sim is not an option once you are approved.

Do I need to sign anything?
Copy link

Yes — you will receive the GFF Live Funded Trader Agreement, which covers your live account. It is separate from the agreement that applied to your sim accounts.

Will I trade on the same platform?
Copy link

In most cases, yes. Your transition email confirms which platforms and data providers are available for your live account. If the platform you use on sim is not available on live yet, we will walk you through switching to one that is.

Breach & Cooldown: What happens if a live account breaches?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

What counts as a breach on my live account?
Copy link

A live account is breached if your balance reaches the drawdown floor. The floor trails your end-of-day closing balance and locks at starting balance + $100.

Example: on a 50K live account ($2,000 drawdown, $0 starting balance) the floor begins at -$2,000. After a day closed at +$800, it sits at -$1,200.

A breached account closes and does not reopen, but there is a clear route back (below).

What happens when my live account breaches?
Copy link

Two things happen:

Your live account closes.
A 21-day cooldown begins, during which new activity is paused — no trading new GFF accounts, no new evaluations, and no payout requests during this window.

If you choose the 50% cash-out instead of going live, the same 21-day cooldown starts as soon as you choose it. Your cash-out payout is still paid during the cooldown. If you go live, the cooldown only applies if your live account breaches.

What happens to my Profit Vault if my live account breaches?
Copy link

The profit carried into the vault is reset back to $0.

Why is the cooldown 21 days?
Copy link

It is a short reset between cycles — a chance to step back and come back fresh and on form for your next account. The 21-day length is in line with the wider industry.

Can I get back to live after a breach?
Copy link

Absolutely. Once your 21-day cooldown ends and you pass a new challenge, the risk team looks at your history with us and can place you straight back into live — so you are earning daily payouts again right away — or have you take a few sim payouts first. It is decided case by case, with a strong track record working in your favour. The same route applies after a cash-out.

How many times can I come back?
Copy link

There is no fixed limit. After each cooldown you can take a new challenge, and the risk team sets your route back. As with any partnership, GFF retains the usual discretion set out in the Trader Agreement.

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

What's the starting balance of my live account?
Copy link

Your live account starts at a $0 balance, with the trading capital fully provided by GFF. The size of your live account is based on your eligible sim accounts at transition — summed together, capped at 150K, GFF's largest live tier. Profit above your starting balance is yours to withdraw, subject to the $500 minimum payout. A payout that takes your balance down to the drawdown floor would breach the account, so leave a buffer above it.

What are the contract limits on my live account?
Copy link

Live accounts have their own contract limits, calibrated to your live drawdown rather than inherited from your sim plan. These are flat: no scaling, no tiers to track.

50K Live: 2 minis / 20 micros
100K Live: 3 minis / 30 micros
150K Live: 5 minis / 50 micros
What's the drawdown on my live account?
Copy link

Your live account uses an end-of-day trailing drawdown. The floor starts at your drawdown amount below your starting balance. It moves up only at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance. Once the floor reaches your starting balance + $100, it locks there and stops moving.

Drawdown by account size:

50K Live: $2,000
100K Live: $3,000
150K Live: $4,500

Example (50K Live, $0 starting balance): the floor starts at -$2,000. Close a day at +$800 and the floor moves to -$1,200. Intraday moves do not change it. Once you close a day at +$2,100 or higher, the floor locks at +$100.

Is there a Daily Loss Limit (DLL) on live?
Copy link

No — live accounts come with no Daily Loss Limit by default, giving you more room to trade your edge. If you would like one as a personal discipline tool, the risk team is happy to set it up on request.

Is there a consistency rule on live?
Copy link

No — there is no consistency rule on live. You have already proven your consistency to get here, so live gives you the freedom to trade without it.

What's the profit split on my live account?
Copy link

90/10 — you keep 90%, from the very first dollar of profit.

While your Profit Vault has a balance, $1,000 is unlocked from it for every $10,000 of live profit, on top of your 90% share.

Live accounts follow the live account profit-sharing structure from day one. Any promotional payout structures or profit-sharing benefits available on simulated accounts do not apply to live accounts unless explicitly stated. Please refer to your Live Account Agreement for the applicable profit-sharing terms.

Can I scale my account size on live?
Copy link

No. Your live account size is set at transition, from your eligible sim account sizes combined and capped at 150K, and stays at that size. There is no scaling plan on live.

Are the trading rules the same as sim?
Copy link

Largely, yes — which keeps things familiar. The news-trading buffer (two minutes around high-impact events) and the no overnight/weekend holding rule carry over from sim. The 1 minute holding rule does not apply on live accounts, but we ask you to trade them with the care of managing actual live capital.

What is a trailing drawdown?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

A trailing drawdown is a loss level that moves upward as your account reaches new highs, but never moves back down. Think of it as a rising floor beneath your account. It follows your profits up but stays put when you give back. If your account equity falls to or below this level, the account is breached.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. This applies to all account types, both challenges and funded accounts. On most plans the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts and Instant (Instant Lite included) it is your starting balance plus $100.

There are two types of trailing drawdown at GOAT Funded Futures.

Trailing EOD (end of day)
Copy link

Used on EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant accounts (Instant Lite included), and on Daily Payouts during the evaluation. The drawdown floor only updates at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
You close the day at $51,500, so your floor moves up to $49,500.
During the next day your equity dips to $49,200 intraday but you close at $50,800. No breach, because the floor is based on your end of day balance, not intraday equity.
Over time, your closing balances push the floor up to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Trailing intraday
Copy link

Used on Daily Payouts funded accounts, and on Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026. The drawdown floor updates in real time, tracking your highest equity point during the session, including unrealised profits on open positions.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
Your equity reaches $51,500 during a trade, so your floor moves up to $49,500 immediately.
If your equity drops to $49,500 at any point, even before closing the trade, the account is breached.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Daily Payouts uses both
Copy link

The evaluation runs end of day trailing and the funded account switches to intraday trailing. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accounts
Copy link

Once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

The Maximum Trailing Intraday Drawdown sets the lowest equity level your account is allowed to reach at any point during a trading session, including on open positions. It trails your highest equity point in real time, meaning as your account reaches new equity highs, the drawdown floor automatically moves up by the same amount. It never moves back down.

Only Daily Payouts funded accounts use intraday trailing. EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and the Daily Payouts evaluation all use end of day trailing, where the floor is calculated from your closing balance and only updates after the trading day ends. Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026 also use intraday trailing, as in the example below.

This is important to understand: the drawdown floor tracks your highest equity, not your closing balance. Even if you give back profits before closing a trade, the floor will have already moved up.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. On Instant Classic the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts it is your starting balance plus $100.

Example (Instant Classic 50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

Your account starts at $50,000, so the max drawdown floor is set at $48,000.
Your equity rises to $51,000 during a trade, so the floor moves up to $49,000.
If your equity drops to $49,000 at any point, the account is breached, even if the trade has not been closed.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Even if your equity later reaches $55,000, the floor stays at $50,000.

On a funded Daily 50K the same mechanics apply, but the floor locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accounts: once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your Instant Classic 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

Payout requirements: winning days, first payout and request windows

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

The requirements before a payout request depend on your account type. Most GFF plans use winning days and monthly request windows. Daily Payouts uses neither, and instead lets you request every 24 hours.

Requirements by account type
Copy link
ACCOUNT TYPE	WINNING DAYS REQUIRED	MINIMUM PROFIT FOR A WINNING DAY	ADDITIONAL FIRST-PAYOUT REQUIREMENT
EOD Funded	7	0.2% of the starting balance	None
1-Day-Pass-Plan Funded	5	0.2% of the starting balance	None
Flex Funded	5	Depends on the account size	None

Daily Payouts Funded	None	Not applicable	First request available 24 hours after your first funded trade
What counts as a winning day?
Copy link

A winning day is a trading day where your net P&L, after commissions and fees, reaches the minimum required amount.

For EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Instant Classic accounts, the requirement is at least 0.2% of the account's starting balance.

For example, a winning day on a 50K account requires at least $100 in net profit.

For Flex accounts, the minimum depends on the account size:

Flex 50K: $250, which is 0.5%
Flex 100K: $400, which is 0.4%
Flex 150K: $450, which is 0.3%

Winning days do not need to be consecutive. They accumulate until you reach the required number for your payout cycle.

Daily Payouts does not use winning days. Payout eligibility on Daily is based on time since your last request, your profit buffer, and the daily progression rule.

When can I request my first payout?
Copy link

For EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Flex funded accounts, you can request your first payout after completing the required winning days and meeting all other applicable payout rules.

For Daily Payouts accounts, you can request 24 hours after you place your first trade on the funded account, with no winning days required. See how the 24 hour payout cycle works.

For Instant accounts, your first reward opens at 6% profit: $1,500 on a 25K, $3,000 on a 50K, $6,000 on a 100K, $9,000 on a 150K. There is no minimum number of days. Later rewards open at 5% profit per cycle: $1,250, $2,500, $5,000 and $7,500. Each reward is capped by the consistency option you chose at checkout: with 15%, $600 / $1,200 / $1,800 / $2,400; with 20%, $1,000 / $2,000 / $3,000 / $4,000 (25K / 50K / 100K / 150K). Rewards are requested within the payout windows, the same as our other plans (Daily Payouts is the only exception).

For Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026, all of the following must be completed before your first payout:

At least 10 calendar days must have passed since your first trade.
You must complete 7 winning days.
Your account must reach the 7% first-payout profit target.
You must meet the 20% consistency rule.
You must complete KYC verification.
What happens after my first payout?
Copy link

A new payout cycle begins after each approved payout.

For Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026, you must also surpass your previous equity high, meaning the account equity level reached before your last withdrawal, before requesting another payout.

Additional recurring-payout requirements may apply depending on when your account was created. Please review the recurring payouts article before submitting another request.

When can I submit a payout request?
Copy link

EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and Instant Classic

Payout requests are submitted through your dashboard during either of the monthly payout windows:

5th to 8th of each month
20th to 23rd of each month

If you become eligible outside a payout window, wait until the next window opens.

Daily Payouts.

There are no payout windows. You can submit your first request 24 hours after you place your first trade on the funded account, and one request every 24 hours after that, on any day of the month.

Before submitting your request
Copy link

Make sure that:

You have completed the required winning days.
You meet any consistency rule that applies to your account.
You meet the minimum payout amount and applicable payout cap.
You satisfy any recurring-payout requirements.
Your KYC verification is complete when required.

On Daily Payouts, check instead that at least 24 hours have passed since your last request, that your balance is above the profit buffer for your size, that at least half of what you are requesting is profit made since your last payout, and that your KYC is complete.

What are the requirements for recurring payouts?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

After an approved payout, a new payout cycle begins on the same account. You must meet the applicable payout requirements again before submitting another request.

What resets after a payout?
Copy link
Your winning-days counter resets to zero.
Your consistency calculation starts fresh for the new payout cycle.

For your first payout, consistency is calculated using the profit accumulated since the account was funded. For later payouts, it is calculated using the profit accumulated during the new cycle after your previous approved payout.

New-profit requirement from your second payout
Copy link

For accounts created after August 7, 2026, the following rule applies from the second payout onward:

At least 50% of the amount you request must come from new profit generated since your previous approved payout.

For example, a $2,000 payout request requires at least $1,000 in new profit during the current payout cycle.

Without this rule, a trader could build a buffer from one or two large days and then keep withdrawing the maximum cap without making anything new.

Eligible example
Copy link

You trade a 50K account to $54,000 and receive a first payout of $2,000, leaving the account at $52,000.

You complete the requirements for the next payout cycle and grow the account to $54,000 again. You have generated $2,000 in new profit since the previous payout, so you satisfy the new-profit requirement for another $2,000 request.

Not-yet-eligible example
Copy link

Using the same example, your account has reached only $52,800. That is $800 in new profit.

A $2,000 request requires at least $1,000 in new profit, so you are not yet eligible to submit that request. Continue trading until the requirement is met.

Instant
Copy link

After your first reward, each new reward opens once you reach 5% profit in the new cycle, requested within the payout windows. There is no winning day requirement. Each reward is capped by the consistency option you chose at checkout, see Instant: specifications, rules and payouts.

Additional requirement for Instant Classic (bought before 18 November 2026)
Copy link

After the first payout on an Instant Classic account, you must surpass your previous equity high, meaning the account equity level reached before your last withdrawal, before requesting another payout.

If your Instant Classic account was created after August 7, 2026, you must satisfy both the previous-equity-high requirement and the new-profit requirement.

Daily Payouts
Copy link

The new-profit requirement above applies to Daily Payouts, where it is called the daily progression rule: at least 50% of what you request must be profit made since your last approved payout.

The rest of this article does not apply to Daily Payouts. There is no winning day requirement and no consistency rule on the funded account, so nothing resets between payouts, and there are no payout windows. You can submit your next request 24 hours after the last one.

What happens if my recurring payout request is declined?
Copy link

A declined request is not a breach and carries no account penalty. Continue trading and submit another request once all requirements are met, during an available payout window on the plans that use them.

Before requesting another payout
Copy link

Make sure that:

You have completed the required winning days.
You meet the consistency rule that applies to your account.
You meet the new-profit requirement if your account is subject to it.
You have surpassed the previous equity high if you trade an Instant Classic account.
Your request meets the minimum payout amount and applicable payout cap.
You submit the request during an available payout window, unless you are on Daily Payouts, which has none.

GOAT Access is a one-phase 50K evaluation with the lowest entry price at GFF: $39 to start, and a one-time $99 activation fee once you pass. There is no time limit, no daily loss limit and no consistency rule in the evaluation.

Where to buy: GOAT Access isn't listed in the dashboard. Get it here: https://goatfundedfutures.com/goat-access

Key benefits

$39 to start the evaluation
No time limit and no minimum trading days. You can pass as soon as you hit the target
No daily loss limit, in evaluation or funded
No consistency rule in the evaluation
End of day trailing max drawdown, which locks at $50,100
Weekly payouts, up to $1,500 per payout
80/20 profit split

Two things to know before you buy

There is an activation fee. GOAT Access is the only GFF plan with one. You pay $99 once you pass, before your funded account is issued.
High impact news trading is not allowed, in the evaluation or on the funded account. This is stricter than Flex and EOD, which allow news trading during the evaluation.

How to pass

Reach the profit target of 5% ($2,500).
Stay above the 4% ($2,000) end of day trailing drawdown, and within the trading rules below.

There is no minimum number of trading days and no time limit. When you pass for the first time, you complete KYC before your funded account is issued.

Maximum drawdown (end of day trailing)

Your maximum drawdown is $2,000 (4%) and trails your end of day balance. It applies in both the evaluation and funded phases. Breaching it is a hard breach, which closes the account.

Your drawdown floor starts at $48,000.
It moves up only when you close a trading day at a new high balance.
Once your end of day balance reaches $52,100, the floor locks at $50,100 (your starting balance + $100) and stops trailing.

Daily loss limit

None. GOAT Access has no daily loss limit in the evaluation or on the funded account, and no maximum daily profit cap.

Consistency rule

Evaluation: none.
Funded: 35%. It is checked when you request a payout.

Payouts

Eligibility: 5 profitable days of at least $150 (0.3%) each.
Buffer: your balance must clear the $2,100 (4.2%) buffer plus the $500 minimum payout.
Minimum request: $500.
Maximum request: $1,500 per payout, the same cap on every payout.
Payout cycle: weekly, once you meet the payout rules again for each request.

Example. You start at $50,000. Once your balance reaches $52,600 or more, with 5 days of $150+ profit, you can request your first payout.

Profit split

80% to you, 20% to GFF.

Holding time: the 1 minute rule

When you pass the evaluation and at each payout request, both of the following must be true:

at least 70% of your closed trades were held longer than 1 minute, and
at least 70% of your net profit came from trades held longer than 1 minute.

If either is not met, we deduct the profit from winning trades held under 1 minute in that cycle from your payout and pay the rest. If that profit is more than the amount you requested, we decline the payout and deduct the requested amount from the account instead. This is not an account breach, and your account stays open.

News trading

Trading high impact news is not allowed, in the evaluation or on the funded account.

Overnight and weekend holding

Not permitted. All positions must be closed before the market closes.

Platforms

GOAT Access is available on DxFeed platforms (Quantower, ATAS, DeepCharts) and TickBlaze. NinjaTrader, Tradovate and TradeSea are not available on GOAT Access.

What happens if I breach?

The evaluation ends. You can reset for $39 or buy a new evaluation.

How does the consistency rule affect payouts?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

The consistency rule ensures that your profits are distributed across multiple trading days rather than depending on one unusually large winning day.

It measures how much of your total profit for the current evaluation or payout cycle came from your most profitable trading day.

How is consistency calculated?
Copy link

Use the following calculation:

Highest-profit day ÷ total profit for the cycle × 100

Your highest-profit day must not be more than the consistency threshold for your account type. Landing exactly on the threshold is allowed.

Consistency thresholds by account type
Copy link
ACCOUNT TYPE	EVALUATION	FUNDED
EOD Challenge	50%	30%
1-Day-Pass-Plan	No consistency rule	35%
Instant	Not applicable	15% or 20%, chosen at checkout and fixed on every reward
Instant Classic (bought before 18 November 2026)	Not applicable	20%
Flex Challenge	50%	No consistency percentage
Daily Payouts	40%	No consistency rule
Worked example
Copy link

You have $3,000 in total profit during the current payout cycle on an EOD funded account. Your highest-profit day is $1,200.

$1,200 ÷ $3,000 × 100 = 40%

The EOD funded consistency threshold is 30%, so you are not yet eligible to request a payout.

If you continue trading until your total profit reaches $4,000, the calculation becomes:

$1,200 ÷ $4,000 × 100 = 30%

You are now within the consistency threshold, provided you have met the other payout requirements.

What happens if I exceed the consistency threshold?
Copy link

You are not disqualified, and exceeding the threshold does not close your account.

You simply cannot request a payout while your highest-profit day is above the applicable threshold. Continue trading and accumulating profit on other days until the highest-profit day represents no more than the allowed percentage of your total profit.

The consistency rule is checked when you request a payout, not continuously while you trade. This gives you the opportunity to bring your account back within the threshold before submitting your request.

Does Flex have a funded consistency rule?
Copy link

Flex funded accounts do not have a numerical consistency percentage. However, all trading must still comply with GFF trading rules and must reflect genuine trading activity. Having no funded consistency percentage does not override prohibited-strategy or anti-gaming rules.

Does Daily Payouts have a funded consistency rule?
Copy link

No. Daily Payouts has no consistency rule on the funded account, so it places no limit on your payouts. The 40% consistency rule applies during the evaluation only, and in practice it means spreading your profit across at least three trading days.
