Help Center / Trading rules / What strategies are prohibited?
What strategies are prohibited?

Updated 9 November 2026Copy link

Every rule below comes down to one question: could this strategy realistically be executed on a live exchange? We assess every account on whether it reflects genuine market trading rather than exploiting our simulated environment. Any strategy that only works because the environment is simulated is not permitted, whether listed below or not. Breaching a rule may result in a warning, profit adjustment, account review, or termination.

Coordinated & linked trading
Copy link

Your trading must be your own and your accounts must operate independently. You may copy your own trades across your own accounts, but copying other users' trades or signals — manually, via copy services, or EAs — is prohibited, as is coordinating trades with other clients, holding opposing or hedged positions across accounts, group trading, trade signaling, or sharing devices, VPS instances, or IPs to enable linked trading. Where linked activity is detected, all accounts and users involved may be suspended.

Risk discipline & position sizing
Copy link

Trade like a professional managing real capital. Disproportionate all-in bets on a single position, account rolling, and erratic sizing swings (one micro on one trade, five minis on the next) may be treated as gambling rather than disciplined trading. Keep your sizing consistent with your strategy and balance.

Exploiting the simulated environment
Copy link

No market manipulation, spoofing, or deceptive conduct designed to distort prices or create false trading conditions. No arbitrage of any kind — latency, hedge, reverse, or rollover. No gap trading around market closures and re-openings, and no profiting from mispriced quotes, feed latency, or external price sources used for an edge.

Scalping & high-frequency abuse
Copy link

Every plan uses the 1 minute rule, checked when you pass an evaluation and at each payout request: at least 70% of your closed trades and at least 70% of your net profit must come from trades held longer than 1 minute. Otherwise the payout is declined and profit from trades under 1 minute is deducted (not a breach). HFT systems, tick scalping, bulk order-entry, and volume inflation are prohibited, and 100+ trades in a single day may trigger a risk review.

Payout & requirement gaming
Copy link

Payouts reward sustainable trading. Earning the bulk of your profit in a single day and then trading the bare minimum to hit the required trading days, or placing token trades to fake activity, may result in the payout being withheld, the concentrated day's profit voided, or the account closed.

News trading
Copy link

News trading is fully allowed on challenge accounts. On funded accounts, you may not open a new position from 2 minutes before until 2 minutes after a scheduled high-impact news release. Holding an existing position through the news is fine, as is managing or closing it.

Unsure whether your strategy is compliant? Ask support before you trade it.

What is the Path to Live?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

The Path to Live is how GFF rewards its most consistent traders with the next step in their journey: a live brokerage account, trading real capital that we provide. Once you qualify, your simulated funded account becomes a live account, you trade with real GFF capital, and you keep 90% of every withdrawal — with the freedom to request payouts daily and no per-payout caps. It is the opportunity to turn proven sim performance into a long-term partnership trading live. Any sim profit you have not yet withdrawn moves into your Profit Vault and unlocks as you profit on live.

Who is the Path to Live for?
Copy link

Every GFF trader. The opportunity is open across every product, EOD Challenge, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant, Flex Challenge and Daily Payouts, and every account size. There is nothing extra to buy and nothing to sign up for: your place is earned purely through your trading on the sim funded account you already hold.

Why does GFF offer this?
Copy link

Because we want to grow alongside the traders who prove they have a genuine edge. The Path to Live is how GFF backs its best performers with real capital on a live brokerage account — the structure used by the most established firms in the industry — and builds a lasting partnership rather than a one-off relationship. For you, that means trading real GFF capital, daily uncapped payouts, and a clear runway to scale your results over time.

Is live trading open?
Copy link

Yes. GFF live accounts are open and the first traders are already trading real GFF capital. There is no launch date to wait for. Transition is decided by the risk team's review of your trading, so the best thing you can do is keep building a consistent track record on your sim funded account.

What happens between approval and activation?
Copy link

Once the risk team approves you, we email you directly with the size and structure of your live account, the Live Funded Trader Agreement, any remaining KYC, and the onboarding steps for the live platform.

While your live account is being set up, your eligible sim accounts are held and trading on them is paused. This keeps the transition clean: your sim track record is locked in and nothing changes on it while the live account opens.

As soon as your live account is active, you are trading real GFF capital with daily uncapped payouts and a 90% profit share.

The email asks you to choose between going live and the 50% cash-out. Reply to the email with your choice. Your eligible sim accounts stay paused until you choose.

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

It depends which limit you hit.

The daily loss limit is a soft breach

Your open positions are closed and trading is paused for the rest of the trading day. It resumes automatically on the next trading day, and your account is not closed. On Flex, the daily loss limit option is a hard breach from the first hit. If you chose it at checkout and your losses for the day reach the limit, the account is closed, in the evaluation or funded. See Can I add a daily loss limit to my Flex account?

The maximum drawdown is a hard breach
Copy link

If your balance or equity falls to or below your drawdown floor, the account is closed immediately. This applies in both the evaluation and funded phases, on every plan.

Can a breached account be reset?
Copy link

A breached evaluation account can be reset up to twice, including on Daily Payouts. A breached Instant account cannot be reset. Funded account resets are available on EOD 50K and 100K accounts only, before your first payout, and are not available on Daily Payouts.

Help Center / Drawdown and loss limits / What does "drawdown lock" or "DD Lock" mean?
What does "drawdown lock" or "DD Lock" mean?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

Important for Funded Accounts
Copy link

The drawdown continues to trail normally as your account reaches new equity highs until it reaches your account's initial starting balance. Once it reaches the starting balance, it locks permanently and will not trail any higher.

On Daily Payouts, Instant and Instant Lite the lock point is your starting balance plus $100, not your starting balance. On a Daily 50K the limit locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100.

Requesting or receiving a payout does not automatically move or lock your drawdown at the starting balance. Your drawdown remains wherever it was before the payout.

Example

On a $50,000 funded account:

Current account balance: $51,000
Current drawdown floor: $49,000

If you request a $1,000 payout, your account balance becomes $50,000, but your drawdown floor remains at $49,000 because it had not yet reached the starting balance before the payout.

This means you now have $1,000 of remaining drawdown room.

Only after the drawdown naturally reaches your account's initial starting balance does it lock permanently.

Once the drawdown has locked, it will remain there even after future payouts. If your balance later falls below that level, the account will be breached.

Does requesting a payout lock my drawdown at the starting balance?
Copy link

No. Requesting or receiving a payout does not change the position of your drawdown floor.

The drawdown continues to trail according to your account rules until it naturally reaches your lock point. Only then does it lock permanently.

If the drawdown has not yet reached the lock point before the payout, it will remain at its current level after the payout.

Multi-Account & Restrictions: Path to Live Restrictions & Multi-Account Rules

Updated 9 October 2026Copy link

How many live accounts can I have at once?
Copy link

One. Your live account is a single consolidated account, built from the sum of your eligible sim account sizes at transition and capped at 150K. After a breach and re-qualification through a new challenge, you earn your next live account through the standard route (see What happens if a live account breaches?).

Can I trade sim and live at the same time?
Copy link

Once you go live, you are all-in on live — which is the point. Every sim funded account with at least one payout is combined into your live account, and any without a payout is closed and refunded. From there, your GFF trading is live, on real capital.

Can my family member trade GFF if I'm on live?
Copy link

Can my family member trade GFF?

No. Members of your immediate family or household may not hold or trade GFF accounts at the same time as you. This applies across every account type and phase — evaluation, funded, and live. Each GFF challenge and account is designed to assess and reward the independent performance of a single trader. When accounts are held by connected individuals, positions can be coordinated, mirrored, or placed in opposition across those accounts in a way that manufactures evaluation passes and payouts not earned through genuine individual trading — and that risk exists whether the balance is simulated or live. To keep the program fair for every trader and the model sustainable, we do not permit connected parties to participate concurrently. Accounts found to be held or traded by related parties in breach of this rule are closed without refund.

Are there country restrictions for live accounts?
Copy link

Yes. The same restricted countries list that applies to sim accounts applies to live. On top of that, our broker runs its own checks when your live account is opened and may decline additional countries at onboarding.

If it turns out a live account is not available in your jurisdiction when you qualify, we will let you know directly and talk through the options. Because the Path to Live is built around moving onto live, continuing together may depend on live being available to you.

Will I be charged anything to transition?
Copy link

No — GFF fully sponsors your account and your transition, so moving onto live costs you nothing. It is our investment in you.

Eligibility: How do I qualify for a live account?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

How do I qualify for a live account?
Copy link

There is no public payout count, dollar target, or numeric milestone that "unlocks" a live account. Our risk team reviews every funded trader based on the full picture, meaning your consistency, how you manage drawdowns, your trading conduct, and your overall risk profile, and identifies when you are ready to move to live capital.

The best path to live is to trade like you intend to keep trading: consistent, disciplined, and risk-aware. Strong trading patterns are noticed regardless of payout count.

Why no public threshold?
Copy link

We want traders focused on developing genuine consistency, not chasing a specific number. A public threshold encourages optimising for the threshold rather than for trading quality, which is the actual signal we look for. Removing it keeps the program aligned around the right thing: building the kind of track record we can trust on live capital.

What does the risk team look at?
Copy link

The full picture of your trading with us, including but not limited to:

Consistency of your trading and your results over time
How you manage drawdowns and risk
Trading conduct, for example how you handle news, position sizing, and behaviour around the daily reset
Your overall risk profile and account history

There is no single metric that triggers transition. It is a holistic call by the risk team.

Can I ask the risk team to move me to live?
Copy link

You do not need to. The team has full visibility into every funded account and reaches out directly when a trader is approved for transition. Asking for review does not move you up the queue, sustained consistency does.

Does my product type affect when I move to live?
Copy link

The transition criterion is the same on every product (EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant, Flex and Daily Payouts): risk team review of your trading history. Copy link

No, the criterion is the same across 25K, 50K, 100K, and 150K accounts. The size of your eventual live account scales with your sim portfolio (see What happens when I transition from sim to live?), but the path itself is consistent.

Will my existing payouts count?
Copy link

Yes, your entire trading history with us is what the risk team reviews. Every approved payout, your consistency, how you have handled drawdowns, your overall risk profile. If you have already built a strong track record, the risk team has visibility into that and factors it into their review.

How will I know I'm being moved to live?
Copy link

We will reach out to you directly by email the moment your account is approved. Your transition notice walks you through the size and structure of your live account, the Live Funded Trader Agreement, any remaining KYC, and step-by-step onboarding for the live platform. Any payout you have already requested is paid as normal first. The email sets out both of your options, your live account or the 50% cash-out, and you choose by replying to it.

Help Center / Rewards and payouts / How are payouts sent and how long do they take?
How are payouts sent and how long do they take?

Updated 19 November 2026Copy link

GFF pays out in two ways: through Rise (Riseworks), a third-party payout platform widely used in the futures prop trading industry, or in crypto (USDT or USDC).

How do I receive my payout?
Copy link

Once you are eligible to request a payout, submit the request through your GFF dashboard and choose Rise or crypto.

On EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and Instant Classic that has to be during an available payout window. Daily Payouts has no windows, so you can request on any day, once every 24 hours.

We then send your payout through the method you chose. You must have completed the required KYC verification before the payout can be completed.

How do crypto payouts work?
Copy link
You can be paid in USDT on the Tron network (TRC20) or USDC on the Ethereum network (ERC20).
You can withdraw up to $1,800 per payout cycle in crypto. The limit counts all your accounts together, not each account separately.
Anything above $1,800 in the same cycle can be withdrawn through Rise.
Check that your wallet address is on the network you choose. Funds sent to an address on the wrong network can be lost.

The same 3% processing fee applies to crypto payouts.

When is KYC required?
Copy link
EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Flex: KYC must be completed before your account is upgraded to the funded stage.
Instant and Instant Classic: KYC must be completed when you become eligible for your first payout.
Daily Payouts: KYC must be completed before your first payout.

The same KYC covers crypto payouts, so you don't need to verify again to be paid in crypto. If your KYC verification is incomplete or requires additional review, your payout may be delayed.

How long does payout processing take?
Copy link

GFF processes payout requests within two business days after the request is submitted.

Weekends and public holidays are not business days. This timeframe covers GFF processing. After that, the payment goes to your Rise account or your crypto wallet.

What should I do if my payout is taking longer?
Copy link

If more than two business days have passed and you have not received an update, contact GFF Support and provide your account details and payout-request information so the team can investigate.

Processing fee for payouts
Copy link

A 3% fee is applied to all payouts, Rise and crypto, to cover payment processing and transaction costs. As a result, the final amount that arrives in your account may be slightly lower than the total shown on your payout certificate.

I believe my account was wrongfully breached, what do I do?

Updated 7 November 2026Copy link

Before contacting support, please check the following:

Log into your dashboard and compare your account equity against the drawdown limit. If your equity is at or below the drawdown level, the breach is correct.
Check whether you had any open positions with unrealized losses that may have pushed your equity below the limit. Drawdown calculations include unrealized P&L, commissions, and fees.
Check whether your account has been inactive for 14 consecutive days, as this will also trigger a breach.

If after reviewing the above you still believe the breach was made in error, contact support with your account ID and a description of what happened.
